candidates.title: Draft clearer order status updates

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare customer-facing order status updates when internal operational data is incomplete or changes frequently.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I’d be interested to hear how others handle customer-facing status updates when internal operational data is incomplete or changes frequently.

ease.reason: A synthetic status row can test a draft, but no supplied reference supports a store connection.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: online shops may pay for clearer order updates; the discussion proves neither payment nor a service market.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can draft from synthetic status changes; live store access and accuracy remain untested.

autonomy.reason: A proposed loop can prepare drafts, but a person must verify changing facts and approve messages; no implementation reference is supplied.

evidence.reason: The post asks about customer-facing updates when operations data is incomplete or changing, but gives no frequency or fields.

candidates.reason: Assessed as a synthetic-data draft experiment; below threshold and duplicate of recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6 on both customer (online shops) and customer-communication workflow.

candidates.title: Notify a restaurant when a web order arrives

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare a notification when a new order is placed on a restaurant website.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I want to build an automated restaurant order notification system using Make.com .

ease.reason: A mock can format an operator-supplied test order, but no supplied reference supports the website trigger or WhatsApp delivery.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small restaurants may pay for timely order alerts; the request establishes neither a buyer market nor payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can format synthetic orders into alert text; live website access and messaging delivery are unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposed loop formats each supplied order, but trigger and delivery are unsupported and a person must verify alerts.

evidence.reason: The request explicitly seeks automated restaurant order notifications, but gives no frequency, fields or corroboration.

candidates.reason: A narrow synthetic-order alert mock is assessable, but the provisional mean is below 6 because live triggering and delivery lack implementation evidence.

rejected.title: Mouse-based flow state protocol
rejected.reason: The post says its author built a protocol, but does not state a repeatable external chore/request for a service; mouse-based biohacking efficacy and safety are also unestablished, so no task or payer is inferred.

rejected.title: Solana copy-trader trade replay
rejected.reason: The Show HN title describes the author replaying trades, not a concrete requested recurring service chore or buyer need. A trading recommendation experiment would add unsupported financial claims.

rejected.title: Voicebots for sales
rejected.reason: The excerpt says voicebots still cannot be used in sales, but does not identify a bounded manual task to automate or requested service; inventing a sales workflow would exceed the evidence.

rejected.title: Need for specialized travel and shopping apps
rejected.reason: This is a broad question about whether apps will be needed, not a concrete existing chore or requested tool task from which to scope an experiment.

rejected.title: Private support ticket access problem
rejected.reason: The only supplied excerpt is a generic troubleshooting prompt, not the poster’s actual problem or task. It cannot support a specific chore without inventing missing context.
